description: Analyzes meaning through inferential roles, commitments, and entitlements in the space of reasons
guiding_thinkers: Robert Brandom, Wilfrid Sellars, John McDowell

assumptions: Meaning is inferential role - to understand a concept is to master its inferential connections
Discourse is normative - a game of giving and asking for reasons
Incompatibility is more fundamental than entailment
Different scorekeepers keep different scores - perspectival structure
Content is not fully determined in advance - retroactive determination possible
Expressive vocabulary makes explicit what is implicit in practice
core_tensions: Commitment vs Entitlement - what you're held to vs. what gives you the right
Undertaking vs Attribution - what you think you're saying vs. what others hear
Default vs Earned entitlement - what gets a free pass vs. what must be proven
Material vs Formal inference - content-based vs. form-based validity
scope_conditions: Applies to discursive practices and conceptual content
Requires social practices of giving and asking for reasons

primary_entities: Commitments - deontic statuses one is held to (not beliefs)
Entitlements - normative authority to make claims
Inferential relations - connections between concepts
Discursive scorekeeping - tracking who is committed to what
Package deals - bundled commitments that come together
relations: Commitment inheritance - downstream commitments from accepting claims
Entitlement inheritance - authority transferred through inference
Incompatibility - positions that cannot be held together
Material consequence - content-based implications
levels_of_analysis: Individual scorekeeping - what each participant tracks
Retrospective determination - how meaning gets fixed over time

change_mechanisms: Discursive move - utterances change normative landscape
Challenge and vindication - testing claims through reasons
Retrospective determination - future practice reveals past commitments
temporal_patterns: Progressive elaboration - concepts develop through use
Retroactive vindication - later developments reveal earlier commitments
Score evolution - normative standings shift through discourse
transformation_processes: Making explicit - expressive vocabulary reveals implicit norms
Conceptual engineering - deliberate revision of inferential roles
Paradigm revision - fundamental restructuring of commitments

key_concepts: Inferential commitment - what accepting a claim puts you on the hook for
Default entitlement - claims presumed okay unless challenged
Material inference - valid by content, not just logical form
Expressive vocabulary - words that make inferential moves explicit
Perspectival gap - difference between speaker intention and hearer attribution
Citation baggage - inherited commitments from endorsed sources
analytical_methods: Scorekeeping analysis - tracking normative statuses
Commitment mapping - what positions commit you to
Incompatibility identification - what you can't hold together
Entitlement auditing - what gives claims their authority
problem_diagnosis: Hidden commitments people don't realize they've incurred
Unearned entitlements - claims made without proper backing
Perspectival gaps causing miscommunication
Package deals forcing undesired commitments
ideal_state: Explicit awareness of inferential commitments
Transparent discursive scorekeeping
Earned entitlements for contested claims
Clear separation of conceptual packages

trait_definitions.trait_description: Analyzing meaning through inferential connections
Focus on normative statuses in discourse
Attention to different scorekeeping perspectives

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Accepting position without acknowledging downstream commitments
critique_patterns.fix: Make explicit that accepting {claim} commits you to {downstream}

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Asserting claim without proper backing or authority
critique_patterns.fix: Identify what would entitle one to claim {assertion}

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Treating speaker intention as equivalent to hearer attribution
critique_patterns.fix: Distinguish what {speaker} undertakes from what {audience} will attribute

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Cherry-picking from citation without inheriting full commitments
critique_patterns.fix: Acknowledge that endorsing {source} brings commitment to {baggage}

historical_context: Developed from Pittsburgh School pragmatism, building on Sellars and extending Kant/Hegel

description: Analyzes social forms through speculative dialectics, emphasizing the broken middle, determinate negation, and the pathologies of both state and civil society
guiding_thinkers: Gillian Rose, Theodor Adorno, G.W.F. Hegel, Walter Benjamin

assumptions: The real is rational and the rational is real - but this is a critical, not affirmative claim
Understanding requires grasping the whole, but totality is always broken and contradictory
Concepts are not merely abstract but have real social existence and power
The 'broken middle' between universal and particular cannot be overcome by theory alone
Identity thinking that subsumes particulars under universals is a form of domination
Critique must be immanent - working from within the contradictions of existing forms
core_tensions: Universal vs Particular - abstract law versus concrete ethical life
State vs Civil Society - political form versus social content
Concept vs Object - thought's claim to grasp reality versus non-identity
Mourning vs Melancholy - working through loss versus endless repetition
scope_conditions: Applies to modern societies with developed legal-political institutions
Requires attention to both institutional forms and lived experience
Focus on how concepts mediate social relations

primary_entities: Sittlichkeit (Ethical Life) - concrete customs, institutions, and practices of a community
Concept (Begriff) - not mere abstraction but the inner structure of reality
Broken Middle - the irreducible gap between universal and particular
Second Nature - social forms that appear natural but are historically constituted
Constellation - non-hierarchical arrangement of concepts that illuminates objects
relations: Determinate Negation - critique that preserves what it negates in transformed form
Mediation - how concepts relate to objects through social practice
Recognition - mutual acknowledgment constituting subjects and institutions
Sublation (Aufhebung) - simultaneous cancellation, preservation, and elevation
levels_of_analysis: Abstract Right - formal property and contract relations
Ethical Life - family, civil society, and state as concrete totality

change_mechanisms: Dialectical development - contradictions drive transformations of social forms
Crisis of mediation - breakdown of institutions that connect universal and particular
Immanent critique - working contradictions through from within
temporal_patterns: Owl of Minerva - philosophy comprehends forms only as they pass
Repetition and difference - historical forms recur but transformed
Retroactive determination - meaning of events fixed by subsequent developments
transformation_processes: Bildung (formation) - education and self-cultivation through estrangement
Work of mourning - acknowledging loss to move beyond it
Speculative reversal - revealing the rational in what appears merely actual

key_concepts: Determinate Negation - negation that specifies what it negates and produces new content
Broken Middle - the unbridgeable gap between law and ethics, universal and particular
Non-identity - the irreducible difference between concept and object
Constellation - arrangement of concepts around an object without reducing it
Second Nature - social forms hardened into apparent naturalness
Absolute Ethical Life - the speculative unity that remains forever broken
analytical_methods: Immanent critique - testing claims against their own standards
Phenomenological reconstruction - tracing shapes of consciousness
Speculative reading - finding the rational kernel in mystified forms
Constellational analysis - arranging concepts to illuminate without subsumption
problem_diagnosis: Juridification - reduction of ethical life to abstract legal categories
Identity thinking - violent subsumption of particulars under universals
Mourning failure - inability to work through historical catastrophe
False reconciliation - premature claims to have overcome contradictions
ideal_state: Speculative experience - thinking that transforms both subject and object
Genuine reconciliation - acknowledging broken middle without false unity
Critical theory as practice - thought that changes what it comprehends
Non-dominating reason - concepts that respect non-identity of objects

trait_definitions.trait_description: Finding rational content in apparently contingent or irrational forms
Criticizing forms by their own internal standards and contradictions
Preserving non-identity against subsumptive totalization

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Universal principles applied without attention to concrete situations
critique_patterns.fix: Show how {universal} requires mediation through {particular_context}

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Treating mediated social forms as natural or immediate
critique_patterns.fix: Trace how {apparent_natural} is historically constituted through {social_process}

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Claiming contradictions resolved when they persist
critique_patterns.fix: Identify the unresolved tension between {thesis} and {antithesis}

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Reducing particulars to instances of abstract categories
critique_patterns.fix: Attend to what in {particular} exceeds or resists {category}

historical_context: Developed from Hegel through Frankfurt School, renewed by Gillian Rose's critique of post-Hegelian thought

description: Analyzes society through class struggle, material conditions, and the contradictions of capitalism
guiding_thinkers: Karl Marx, Friedrich Engels, Antonio Gramsci, Rosa Luxemburg

assumptions: Material conditions of production determine social consciousness
History progresses through class struggle and modes of production
Social being determines consciousness, not vice versa
Capitalism contains internal contradictions leading to its transformation
Human essence is realized through social labor and production
Ideas and culture reflect and legitimize material class relations
core_tensions: Forces vs Relations of Production - technological capacity versus social organization
Use Value vs Exchange Value - concrete utility versus abstract market value
Labor vs Capital - those who produce versus those who own
Base vs Superstructure - economic foundation versus ideological forms
scope_conditions: Applies to societies with developed division of labor and private property
Cannot explain pre-class societies or post-class communist society fully
Requires material production as basis of social life

primary_entities: Classes - groups defined by relationship to means of production
Mode of Production - unity of forces and relations defining an epoch
Commodity - product with both use and exchange value for market
Labor Power - human capacity to work, sold as commodity
Capital - self-expanding value through exploitation of labor
relations: Exploitation - extraction of surplus value from labor
Class antagonism - structural opposition of class interests
Commodity exchange - market-mediated social relations
Base-superstructure determination - economic shapes political/ideological
levels_of_analysis: Economic base - forces and relations of production
Political superstructure - state, law, and institutions

change_mechanisms: Contradiction-driven crisis - internal contradictions generate systemic crises
Class struggle - conflict between classes drives historical change
Mode of production transformation - productive forces outgrow relations
temporal_patterns: Historical materialism - modes of production succeed through revolution
Crisis cycles - periodic crises of overproduction and profitability
Tendential laws - long-term trends like falling rate of profit
transformation_processes: Revolution - fundamental restructuring of class relations
Proletarianization - expansion of wage labor relations
Primitive accumulation - violent separation from means of production

key_concepts: Surplus value - value created by workers beyond their wages
Alienation - separation from product, process, species-being, and others
False consciousness - ideology that misrepresents real conditions
Commodity fetishism - social relations appear as relations between things
Primitive accumulation - violent separation from means of production
Reserve army of labor - unemployed maintaining wage pressure
analytical_methods: Dialectical materialism - analyzing contradictions in material conditions
Historical materialism - tracing modes of production through history
Class analysis - identifying class positions and interests
Critique of political economy - revealing capitalism's inner workings
problem_diagnosis: Exploitation of labor by capital
Alienation from human creative essence
Ideological mystification of class relations
Anarchic, crisis-prone production for profit
ideal_state: Classless society with collective ownership
From each according to ability, to each according to need
Free association of producers controlling their labor
End of prehistory, beginning of human history

trait_definitions.trait_description: Method of analysis through contradictions and their resolution
Grounding analysis in material conditions and production
Critique of existing social relations and ideology

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Abstract categories without class content
critique_patterns.fix: Specify class position of {actors} and interests in {process}

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Ideas or consciousness as prime mover
critique_patterns.fix: Ground {ideological_form} in material conditions of {base}

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Treating historical forms as eternal
critique_patterns.fix: {Category} specific to {mode_of_production}, not universal

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Change through will alone without material conditions
critique_patterns.fix: Revolution requires both objective conditions and subjective organization

historical_context: Emerged in 19th century industrial capitalism, evolved through 20th century revolutionary movements

description: Analyzes global capitalism as a system of imperialist exploitation where the contradictions between colonized/semi-colonized nations and metropolitan powers supersede contradictions within individual nations, requiring armed struggle and revolutionary nationalism as paths to liberation. Synthesizes Marxist class analysis with anti-colonial struggle, arguing that the primary contradiction of our era is between imperialism and oppressed nations, and that true proletarian internationalism means supporting third-world revolutionary movements against Euro-American hegemony. Emphasizes that liberation requires not merely capturing state power but dismantling colonial economic structures, achieving genuine sovereignty over resources and production, and building socialism adapted to semi-feudal and colonized material conditions rather than importing European models.
guiding_thinkers: Mao, Mariategui, Che Guevara, Fidel Castro, Ho Chi Mihn

assumptions: The primary contradiction in the contemporary era is between imperialist nations (the metropole) and colonized/semi-colonized nations (the periphery), superseding class contradictions within individual nations; the global proletariat is predominantly located in the Third World where super-exploitation concentrates revolutionary potential

Underdevelopment is not a pre-capitalist residue but actively produced through imperialist extraction—metropolitan accumulation requires peripheral immiseration; capitalism in colonized nations develops as comprador capitalism serving foreign interests rather than national development, creating semi-feudal and semi-colonial material conditions that demand revolutionary strategies distinct from European proletarian models

National liberation and socialist construction are dialectically unified—genuine independence requires breaking imperialist economic chains through revolutionary violence, not reformist gradualism; bourgeois nationalism in colonized contexts can serve progressive anti-imperialist goals when aligned with peasant masses, though it must be transcended toward proletarian leadership to prevent neocolonial capture

The international division of labor under imperialism transfers surplus value from periphery to core through unequal exchange, debt mechanisms, and monopoly pricing; First World workers benefit materially from super-exploitation of Third World labor, creating a labor aristocracy whose reformism objectively serves imperialism—true proletarian internationalism means metropolitan workers supporting peripheral armed struggles even against their immediate material interests

Revolutionary transformation in semi-colonial societies requires protracted people's war mobilizing the peasantry as the primary revolutionary force, surrounding cities from the countryside both militarily and politically; state power must be seized through armed struggle not parliamentary means, as colonial and comprador states exist fundamentally as enforcement mechanisms for imperialist extraction and cannot be reformed into instruments of liberation
core_tensions: National Liberation vs Socialist Construction - revolutionary movements must simultaneously wage anti-imperialist struggle while building productive forces in semi-feudal conditions, creating tension between immediate military necessity and long-term economic transformation that classical Marxism never theorized for societies lacking industrial proletariats

Revolutionary Nationalism vs Proletarian Internationalism - authentic anti-colonial struggle requires mobilizing populations through national identity and sovereignty claims, yet risks reproducing bourgeois nationalism unless subordinated to international solidarity with all colonized peoples against the metropolitan core, demanding careful navigation between necessary patriotism and chauvinist deviation

Peasant Masses vs Industrial Proletariat - in colonized and semi-colonized nations the revolutionary subject consists primarily of peasantry rather than urban workers, contradicting orthodox Marxism's privileging of industrial labor while requiring theoretical innovation to understand how agrarian populations can lead socialist transformation without replicating capitalist modernization

Comprador Bourgeoisie vs National Bourgeoisie - colonial economic structures create splits within capitalist classes between those integrated into imperialist circuits (comprador) and those with interests in sovereign development (national), generating tactical questions about temporary alliances while maintaining that ultimate liberation requires transcending all bourgeois forces

Autonomous Development vs Integration into World System - breaking from colonial extraction requires building independent productive capacity, yet complete autarky proves materially impossible, forcing choices between selective engagement with world markets that risks resubordination and isolation that limits technological advancement and economic growth
scope_conditions: Societies subjected to formal colonialism or neocolonial economic domination where national sovereignty remains compromised by imperialist extraction of surplus through unequal exchange, debt mechanisms, or military occupation

Revolutionary situations in semi-feudal or semi-colonial formations where comprador bourgeoisie mediates metropolitan capital's interests, requiring protracted people's war or national liberation struggle rather than urban insurrection

Historical conjunctures where the primary contradiction between oppressed nations and imperialism supersedes internal class contradictions, making cross-class national united fronts strategically necessary for anti-imperialist struggle

Peripheral zones of capital accumulation where subsistence agriculture, extractive mono-economies, and technologically dependent industrialization prevent autonomous capitalist development, necessitating delinking from world market integration

Geopolitical contexts where metropolitan working classes benefit materially from imperialist super-profits, making third-world peasantry and semi-proletariat the principal revolutionary subjects rather than European-style industrial proletariat

primary_entities: Comprador Class - indigenous bourgeoisie serving as intermediaries for foreign capital, facilitating extraction while blocking autonomous development through integration into imperialist supply chains and financial circuits

Revolutionary Nation - semi-colonial or colonized peoples organized as collective subjects of liberation, whose unity across class lines becomes primary in anti-imperialist struggle before internal class contradictions can be resolved

Imperialist Bloc - metropolitan powers (US, Western Europe, Japan) and their satellite states that maintain global exploitation through military bases, international financial institutions, unequal exchange, and neocolonial debt mechanisms

National Bourgeoisie - contradictory class fraction in colonized nations possessing both anti-imperialist potential (when seeking autonomous industrialization) and comprador tendencies (when accepting subordinate integration into world system)

Peasant-Proletarian Alliance - revolutionary subject uniting agricultural producers and emerging industrial workers in semi-feudal societies, replacing the classical urban proletariat as vanguard due to peripheral capitalism's distorted development
relations: Imperial extraction - metropole siphons surplus through unequal exchange, debt servitude, and comprador class collaboration, transferring value from periphery to center while maintaining productive underdevelopment

Revolutionary class alliance - national bourgeoisie, peasantry, urban workers, and lumpenproletariat unite against foreign imperialism and domestic compradors, with contradictions among the people subordinated to principal contradiction with imperialism

Colonial dependency - productive capacities shaped by imperial needs rather than internal development, creating monoculture economies, technological dependence, and structural inability to complete industrialization

Armed struggle-mass line dialectic - guerrilla warfare both embodies and generates revolutionary consciousness in the peasantry, transforming passive subjects of empire into active makers of their liberation

Tricontinental solidarity - oppressed nations constitute a global revolutionary zone encircling and strangling metropolitan capitalism, with their national liberation struggles objectively weakening imperialism regardless of their ideological completeness
levels_of_analysis: International - Global system of imperial extraction where metropolitan centers accumulate through unequal exchange, debt servitude, and military domination of peripheral nations, creating a world divided between oppressor and oppressed nations rather than simply capitalist and socialist blocs

National - Semi-colonial or colonized nation-states whose comprador bourgeoisie and feudal remnants collaborate with imperialism, making national liberation and sovereignty over productive forces the precondition for any genuine socialist transformation

Class within colonial context - Peasantry and semi-proletariat as revolutionary subjects in colonized nations, where classical industrial proletariat is underdeveloped due to imperialist prevention of independent industrialization, requiring analysis of how colonial extraction reshapes class composition

Mode of production articulation - Intersection of pre-capitalist relations (feudalism, communal production) with imposed capitalist extraction, creating hybrid formations where imperialism profits from maintaining 'backwardness' rather than developing productive forces

Armed struggle and base areas - Liberated zones where revolutionary power establishes alternative economic relations outside imperial control, demonstrating that state power must be seized through protracted people's war to break dependency rather than through parliamentary means in comprador states

change_mechanisms: National liberation struggle - Armed revolutionary movements led by peasant-worker alliances and revolutionary intellectuals that physically expel colonial/neocolonial forces, seize state power, and establish sovereignty over national resources; change occurs through protracted people's war that builds dual power in the countryside, mobilizes the peasantry as the revolutionary backbone in semi-feudal societies, and progressively encircles urban centers of comprador bourgeois power

Breaking comprador chains - Structural transformation of economies through expropriation of foreign capital, land reform that eliminates feudal-colonial relations of production, nationalization of extractive industries, and construction of independent industrial capacity; change requires severing dependent integration into imperialist accumulation circuits and building self-reliant productive forces aligned with popular consumption rather than metropolitan markets

Revolutionary nationalism superseding class reductionism - Popular mobilization against imperialism that unites multiple classes (peasants, workers, petty bourgeoisie, national bourgeoisie) under anti-colonial struggle, recognizing that the primary contradiction is between nation and empire rather than purely internal class antagonisms; the nation itself becomes a proletarianized subject exploited by imperialist powers, requiring nationalist consciousness as the vehicle for socialist transformation

Tricontinental solidarity networks - Coordinated resistance across the Global South that provides material support for liberation movements, shares military-political strategy, creates alternative trade arrangements outside imperialist circuits, and establishes ideological independence from both US capitalism and Soviet revisionism; change accelerates through synchronized struggles that strain imperialism's capacity for counter-insurgency and create liberated zones that demonstrate socialist possibility

Cultural revolution against colonial mentality - Transformation of consciousness through mass campaigns that combat internalized colonial ideology, valorize indigenous knowledge systems and productive practices, replace comprador education with revolutionary pedagogy, and forge new socialist subjects capable of collective self-determination; lasting change requires destroying the psychological infrastructure of dependency alongside its material structures
temporal_patterns: Revolutionary time versus colonial time - National liberation movements operate on extended timescales of protracted people's war and base-building that resist imperialist demands for immediate capitulation or integration, creating temporalities oriented toward multi-generational transformation rather than capital's cycles of accumulation and crisis

Uneven development as temporal weapon - Imperial centers accelerate their own development by freezing peripheries in permanent 'backwardness' through debt, extraction, and comprador relations, requiring revolutionary movements to simultaneously combat feudal remnants and imperialist penetration across non-synchronous historical stages

Cycles of neo-colonial reintegration - Independence movements repeatedly face sabotage, coup, and economic strangulation that force resubordination to imperial markets within 10-30 year cycles, demonstrating that formal sovereignty without economic transformation merely resets the timeline of exploitation under new national flags

Accumulation of revolutionary consciousness through defeat - Colonial subjects develop anti-imperialist understanding not linearly but through ruptures of massacre, betrayal, and failed reformism that compress decades of theoretical development into moments of clarity about the impossibility of peaceful transition or developmental gradualism

Telescoping of historical stages - Semi-colonial societies must simultaneously wage bourgeois-democratic revolution against feudalism and proletarian revolution against imperialism in compressed timeframes, collapsing European centuries into decades through revolutionary voluntarism and mass mobilization rather than awaiting capitalist maturation
transformation_processes: Revolutionary war as protracted strategy - Liberation unfolds through prolonged people's war that builds dual power in liberated zones, transforms social relations during the struggle itself, and gradually encircles metropolitan-controlled cities from a countryside mobilized through land reform and mass participation. The transformation process is simultaneously military (defeating colonial forces), economic (breaking comprador bourgeoisie's control over resources), and cultural (forging new revolutionary consciousness through combat), with each liberated territory becoming a laboratory for socialist construction adapted to semi-colonial material conditions rather than imposed European models.

National democratic revolution progressing to socialist construction - Transformation proceeds through stages where anti-imperialist united fronts first achieve national sovereignty and expropriate foreign capital, then advance to collectivization and planned economy as feudal/comprador classes are eliminated. The process requires maintaining revolutionary vigilance against bourgeois restorationism while developing productive forces under conditions of imperialist encirclement, often necessitating temporary alliances with national bourgeoisie who can be won to anti-colonial struggle before being superseded in transition to socialism.

Breaking dependency through delinking and self-reliance - Transformation requires conscious decoupling from imperialist world-system through import-substitution, South-South cooperation, and development of autonomous technological capacity rather than accepting dependent integration. The process demands initial sacrifice of consumption levels to build heavy industry, agricultural mechanization, and defensive military capacity, while simultaneously cultivating revolutionary internationalism that supports other liberation movements rather than seeking accommodation with metropolitan powers or reproduction of exploitative relations with weaker nations.

Cultural revolution eliminating colonial mentalities - Transformation necessitates ongoing struggle against internalized colonialism, comprador ideology, and feudal consciousness that persist after formal political independence. This unfolds through mass campaigns combining ideological education, criticism-self-criticism sessions, and practical participation in production that break down mental/manual labor divisions inherited from colonial caste systems, while creating new revolutionary culture rooted in peasant/worker experience rather than metropolitan aesthetic forms or pre-colonial traditions fetishized by reactionary nationalism.

Tricontinental solidarity as mutual transformation - Liberation advances through coordinated struggle across the colonial world where victories in one nation weaken imperialism's global system and create material/ideological support for movements elsewhere. The process involves practical sharing of guerrilla tactics, training cadres across movements, and coordinated economic resistance through commodity cartels and alternative trading blocs, while ideologically constructing shared identity as the 'Third World' or 'Global South' that supersedes both national boundaries and orthodox Marxist privileging of European proletariat as revolutionary vanguard.

key_concepts: Comprador bourgeoisie - the indigenous ruling class in colonized/semi-colonized nations whose wealth depends on facilitating imperialist extraction, mediating between metropolitan capital and local resources/labor, and whose interests are structurally aligned with maintaining neo-colonial dependency rather than national development

Unequal exchange - the systematic transfer of value from periphery to core through terms of trade where peripheral raw materials are undervalued while metropolitan manufactured goods are overvalued, perpetuating accumulation in imperialist centers regardless of nominal political independence

Revolutionary nationalism - anti-imperialist struggle that unites peasants, workers, and national bourgeoisie against foreign domination, distinguished from bourgeois nationalism by its trajectory toward socialism once comprador elements are eliminated and productive forces brought under sovereign control

Semi-feudal economy - social formation where pre-capitalist relations (landlordism, usury, tribute) persist not as archaic remnants but as structures actively maintained by imperialism to facilitate extraction, requiring agrarian revolution and land redistribution as prerequisites for socialist construction

Principal contradiction - the primary antagonism (imperialism vs oppressed nations) that subordinates all others in a given historical moment, determining revolutionary strategy by identifying which struggle must be resolved before internal class contradictions can be successfully addressed

Protracted people's war - military strategy adapted to semi-feudal conditions where revolutionary forces build base areas in the countryside, mobilize the peasantry through land reform, encircle cities from rural strongholds, and achieve victory through prolonged attrition rather than urban insurrection
analytical_methods: National liberation class analysis - mapping class fractions in semi-colonial societies to identify which classes align with imperialism (comprador bourgeoisie, landlords) versus which can participate in anti-imperialist united fronts (national bourgeoisie, peasantry, lumpenproletariat), recognizing that class positions are determined by relationship to imperial extraction rather than purely internal production relations

Unequal exchange calculation - quantifying flows of value from periphery to core through mechanisms like debt servicing, profit repatriation, unequal terms of trade, technology rents, and brain drain to demonstrate how accumulation in metropolitan centers structurally depends on transfer from colonized zones, revealing that third-world poverty and first-world wealth are dialectically produced

Revolutionary situation assessment - analyzing the specific contradictions and balance of forces in semi-feudal/semi-colonial societies to determine whether conditions favor protracted people's war (landlord-peasant antagonism dominant), urban insurrection (comprador capitalism developed), or anti-colonial united front (settler-colonialism or occupation), adapting strategy to concrete conditions rather than importing European models

Comprador identification - tracing flows of capital, political allegiance, and ideological orientation to identify which national elites function as intermediaries for foreign capital, differentiating between national bourgeoisie who may temporarily ally with revolutionary forces and compradors whose class interests are inseparable from imperial domination

Sovereignty forensics - examining actual versus nominal control over currency issuance, resource extraction rights, military bases, debt conditions, trade agreements, and monetary policy to determine the real degree of national independence, revealing how neocolonial arrangements maintain extraction after formal decolonization through financial and institutional mechanisms
problem_diagnosis: Problems originate in the structural position of nations within the imperialist world-system, where comprador bourgeoisies collaborate with metropolitan capital to extract surplus from colonized territories through unequal exchange, debt mechanisms, and resource extraction, creating underdevelopment as the dialectical counterpart to metropolitan accumulation rather than as a stage to be overcome through capitalist modernization

The primary contradiction manifests between oppressed nations and imperialism rather than between proletariat and bourgeoisie within individual nations, meaning that national liberation struggles led by revolutionary nationalist movements (incorporating workers, peasants, and patriotic intellectuals) take precedence over traditional working-class politics modeled on European experience in semi-feudal and colonized contexts

Neo-colonial economic structures persist after formal independence through continued metropolitan control of finance, technology, markets, and military power, with international institutions (IMF, World Bank, WTO) serving as instruments of collective imperialism that enforce debt peonage, structural adjustment, and integration into disadvantageous terms of trade while local comprador classes benefit from their intermediary position

Revolutionary consciousness emerges not from industrial proletarian experience but from the concrete reality of colonial violence, land dispossession, cultural destruction, and super-exploitation, requiring revolutionary theory to be adapted to specific semi-feudal formations, peasant-based economies, and the particular colonial history of each oppressed nation rather than mechanically applying European models

Reformist and revisionist movements are diagnosed as objectively serving imperialism when they advocate peaceful transition, parliamentary roads, or integration into the world market, because these paths leave intact the extractive relationship between periphery and core while creating illusions that mask the necessity of armed struggle and complete rupture with imperialist economic structures
ideal_state: Complete dismantling of imperialist economic structures including comprador bourgeoisie, foreign monopolies, and debt mechanisms that extract surplus from periphery to core. National liberation movements establish genuine sovereignty over resources, production, and finance, with state power wielded to redirect surplus toward internal development, breaking chains of unequal exchange that maintain underdevelopment.

Revolutionary construction of socialism adapted to semi-feudal and colonial material conditions through mass line and people's war, not mechanical transplantation of European models. Peasant-worker alliances lead transformation of agriculture and industry simultaneously, with literacy campaigns, land reform, and self-reliant development strategies that prioritize meeting people's needs over integration into world capitalist system.

Proletarian internationalism manifested as material solidarity among oppressed nations forming united front against imperialism, sharing technology and resources outside capitalist markets, and metropolitan workers supporting third-world liberation rather than defending their parasitic share of super-profits. Anti-colonial struggle becomes primary contradiction superseding reformist trade unionism in imperial core.

Cultural revolution to eliminate colonial mentality, comprador ideology, and feudal remnants while forging new socialist consciousness rooted in national liberation and collective self-determination. Education, art, and theory develop from masses' revolutionary practice rather than imported intellectual frameworks, creating knowledge systems that serve liberation not Eurocentric universalism.

Multipolar world system where formerly colonized nations exercise genuine self-determination in development paths, control terms of trade and technology transfer, and build regional cooperation outside dollar hegemony. Revolutionary states encircle and squeeze imperialist powers through resource sovereignty, alternative institutions, and support for insurgencies, creating conditions for global transition from capitalism.

trait_definitions.trait_description: Analyzes material conditions through the lens of colonial extraction and imperial value transfer, recognizing that relations of production in colonized zones are structured by their subordination to metropolitan accumulation rather than following autonomous capitalist development
trait_items: Traces flows of surplus value from periphery to core through unequal exchange, debt servicing, and resource extraction
Identifies comprador bourgeoisie as a class whose accumulation depends on facilitating imperial penetration rather than national development
Analyzes semi-feudal relations not as pre-capitalist residues but as actively maintained by imperialism to prevent autonomous industrialization
Examines how colonial division of labor assigns extractive and agricultural roles to periphery while reserving manufacturing and finance to core
Recognizes that 'underdevelopment' is not absence of development but a specific form produced through systematic value transfer

trait_definitions.trait_description: Treats national liberation as prerequisite to socialist construction in colonized contexts, analyzing nationalist movements not as bourgeois deviations but as necessary stages in rupturing imperial chains and establishing sovereignty over productive forces
trait_items: Distinguishes revolutionary nationalism that confronts imperialism from reactionary nationalism that serves it
Analyzes how imperial domination makes the entire colonized nation, across classes, objectively opposed to foreign capital
Recognizes national bourgeoisie's contradictory position: potentially progressive against imperialism, ultimately limited by class interests
Examines peasantry as revolutionary force in semi-feudal societies where proletariat is underdeveloped
Treats cultural decolonization and recovery of indigenous knowledge systems as material forces in revolutionary struggle

trait_definitions.trait_description: Analyzes revolutionary transformation as requiring protracted armed struggle against both domestic comprador classes and imperial military forces, rejecting parliamentary roads and peaceful transitions as ineffective against entrenched colonial violence
trait_items: Examines guerrilla warfare as strategy appropriate to asymmetric power relations between liberation movements and imperial armies
Analyzes how armed struggle creates liberated zones where alternative social relations can be constructed during conflict
Treats people's war as process that transforms consciousness through revolutionary practice, not merely military campaign
Recognizes that imperial powers will use violence to maintain extraction, making armed defense of sovereignty necessary
Examines how protracted conflict tests and purifies revolutionary forces, eliminating opportunists and compromisers

trait_definitions.trait_description: Analyzes revolutionary internationalism as horizontal alliance among oppressed nations rather than vertical leadership by European parties, treating anti-imperialist struggles across Asia, Africa, and Latin America as strategically linked fronts against common enemy
trait_items: Identifies contradictions between metropolitan working classes and third world liberation as metropolitan labor benefits from imperial superprofits
Examines how victories in one peripheral zone weaken imperialism globally by disrupting extraction and emboldening other movements
Analyzes tactical and strategic lessons from successful liberation struggles as directly transferable across colonized contexts
Treats Soviet revisionism and social-imperialism as betrayals of genuine internationalism in favor of great power competition
Recognizes that encirclement by imperialism requires coordinated resistance rather than isolated national struggles

trait_definitions.trait_description: Analyzes control over natural resources, land, and productive infrastructure as central to genuine independence, treating nationalization and land reform not as economic policies but as dismantling colonial extraction mechanisms
trait_items: Examines how imperial contracts, debt obligations, and 'development' loans function as mechanisms to maintain resource access after formal decolonization
Analyzes land reform as breaking power of landlord classes allied with imperialism while creating peasant base for revolution
Treats nationalization of extractive industries as recovering surplus for domestic accumulation rather than metropolitan enrichment
Recognizes that nominal political independence without economic sovereignty leaves colonial relations intact
Examines how control over resources enables autonomous industrialization and breaks dependency on manufactured imports

trait_definitions.trait_description: Analyzes socialist development in colonized contexts as requiring strategies appropriate to semi-feudal material conditions and ongoing imperial threat rather than mechanically applying European or Soviet models designed for advanced capitalist societies
trait_items: Examines how absence of developed proletariat requires mobilizing peasantry as primary revolutionary class
Analyzes collectivization as strategy for transforming scattered peasant production while avoiding Soviet coercive errors
Treats self-reliance not as autarky but as strategic necessity when integration into world market means continued exploitation
Recognizes need for transitional programs that address immediate survival while building toward socialist relations
Examines how encirclement by imperialism shapes possibility and pace of socialist transformation

trait_definitions.trait_description: Analyzes working classes in imperial centers as objectively benefiting from superexploitation of colonized labor through higher wages, social wages, and access to cheap commodities, making them unreliable allies and often active supporters of imperialism
trait_items: Traces how superprofits extracted from colonies enable higher wages in metropole without reducing capitalist profits
Examines social-democratic welfare states as funded by imperial extraction, creating material stake in colonialism
Analyzes how trade unions in imperial centers often support protectionist and chauvinist policies against third world workers
Recognizes that revolutionary potential has shifted from metropolitan proletariat to colonized masses
Treats worker complicity in imperialism as structural position rather than mere ideological failure

trait_definitions.trait_description: Analyzes Soviet peaceful coexistence, Euro-communist parliamentarism, and Trotskyist dogmatism as betrayals that subordinate third world liberation to European strategic interests, requiring sharp ideological struggle against these deviations
trait_items: Examines how Soviet state-to-state diplomacy sacrificed revolutionary movements to maintain détente with imperialism
Analyzes Khrushchev's peaceful coexistence as abandoning armed struggle precisely when liberation movements were advancing
Treats Trotskyist dismissal of peasant revolutions as Eurocentric dogma that denies revolutionary agency to colonized
Recognizes that revisionist parties in periphery function as safety valves preventing radical rupture with imperialism
Examines how revisionism preserves substance of colonial relations while claiming anti-imperialist rhetoric

trait_definitions.trait_description: Analyzes revolutionary knowledge as produced through dialectical relationship between cadre and masses, where systematic investigation of concrete conditions grounds theory rather than importing European formulas to disparate contexts
trait_items: Treats 'from the masses, to the masses' as method for discovering revolutionary strategies appropriate to specific material conditions
Examines how urban intellectual cadre must learn from peasant knowledge of land, local power structures, and survival strategies
Analyzes social investigation as producing concrete analysis rather than applying abstract schemas
Recognizes that masses generate revolutionary innovations through practical struggle that theorists must systematize
Treats criticism and self-criticism as mechanisms for correcting deviation from mass line

trait_definitions.trait_description: Analyzes Western claims of universal civilization as ideological cover for imperial domination, recognizing need to recover indigenous forms of social organization, knowledge production, and cultural practice suppressed by colonialism
trait_items: Examines how Enlightenment universalism functioned as justification for colonial 'civilizing mission' while destroying non-European societies
Analyzes development discourse as continuation of colonial hierarchy that treats European modernity as only legitimate path
Treats indigenous communal land tenure, collective decision-making, and reciprocal economies as resources for socialist construction
Recognizes that decolonization requires epistemic rupture with Western categories that naturalize imperial power
Examines how cultural imperialism through education, language, and media maintains colonial mentality after formal independence

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Analysis privileges industrial working class contradictions in imperialist centers over colonial/neo-colonial extraction relations, treating third-world struggles as derivative rather than primary
critique_patterns.fix: Reframe {class_analysis} to recognize that imperialism transfers surplus from colonized to colonizing nations, making metropolitan 'proletariat' materially invested in empire. Replace focus on {metropolitan_contradiction} with analysis of how {colonial_extraction_mechanism} structures global class relations and creates a labor aristocracy in the core.

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Assumes societies must pass through European capitalist development before socialism is possible, ignoring how imperialism prevents autonomous accumulation and how semi-feudal conditions require revolutionary rather than bourgeois-democratic transformation
critique_patterns.fix: Replace stagist sequence {feudalism→capitalism→socialism} with analysis of how imperialism arrests development through {specific_extraction_mechanism}. Show how {revolutionary_movement} must simultaneously combat both pre-capitalist relations and imperialist domination without waiting for bourgeois consolidation, as demonstrated in {historical_case}.

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Treats post-colonial flag independence as genuine sovereignty while ignoring continued economic subordination through debt, unequal exchange, and comprador class collaboration
critique_patterns.fix: Distinguish formal political independence from actual sovereignty by examining {nation}'s continued dependence on {metropolitan_power} through {mechanism: debt servitude/resource extraction/technology monopolies}. Show how {comprador_class} administers neo-colonial extraction and how {economic_structure} remains oriented toward external accumulation rather than internal development.

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Treats 'working class' as homogeneous global category, obscuring how imperialism creates material divisions between metropolitan labor aristocracy benefiting from super-exploitation and actually-existing global proletariat in colonized zones
critique_patterns.fix: Replace abstract 'proletariat' with stratified analysis distinguishing: (1) labor aristocracy in {imperialist_nation} whose wages include super-profit from colonies, (2) actually revolutionary proletariat in {colonized_nation} facing both capitalist exploitation and national oppression, and (3) {semi-proletarianized_class} retaining ties to pre-capitalist production. Show how {struggle_example} reveals these material divisions.

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Suggests electoral or gradual paths to power in neo-colonial contexts where comprador state apparatus exists precisely to prevent transformation threatening imperialist interests
critique_patterns.fix: Demonstrate that {comprador_state} in {nation} is structurally committed to {imperialist_power}'s interests through {mechanism: military ties/debt obligations/elite education}. Show how {failed_reformist_attempt} was crushed through {intervention_method}, proving that liberation requires armed struggle to dismantle {specific_apparatus} and establish revolutionary state capable of resisting imperialist pressure, as in {successful_example}.

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Focuses on developing productive forces without addressing who controls technology, capital goods production, and terms of trade—assuming development is possible within imperialist division of labor
critique_patterns.fix: Show how {development_program} attempted to increase production while remaining dependent on {imperialist_nation} for {capital_goods/technology/markets}, resulting in {failure_mode}. Contrast with {revolutionary_case} that achieved sovereignty over {key_sector} by {breaking_dependency_mechanism}, demonstrating that genuine development requires control over entire production cycle, not just final assembly.

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Analyzes colonial domination primarily through cultural/identity categories rather than material extraction relations, separating 'cultural imperialism' from economic structures
critique_patterns.fix: Connect cultural forms {ideology/education_system/media} to material function of reproducing {specific_class_relation} in service of {extraction_mechanism}. Show how {cultural_phenomenon} is not autonomous 'domination' but concrete ideological apparatus legitimizing {comprador_class}'s administration of {economic_structure}. Demonstrate that cultural decolonization requires dismantling {material_base} that cultural forms express.

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Ignores peasantry as revolutionary force in semi-feudal societies where urban proletariat is small, treating rural masses as backward or counter-revolutionary rather than primary base for liberation
critique_patterns.fix: Recognize that in {semi-colonized_nation}, peasantry constitutes {percentage} of population subjected to {landlord_relation} and {imperialist_extraction_method}. Show how {revolutionary_movement} organized peasant base by addressing {land_question} and linking anti-feudal struggle to anti-imperialist struggle. Contrast with {failed_urban_strategy} that ignored countryside, demonstrating peasantry's central role in protracted people's war in conditions of {specific_social_formation}.

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Treats IMF, World Bank, WTO as neutral development institutions rather than instruments of imperialist domination imposing structural adjustment that reproduces dependency
critique_patterns.fix: Expose how {institution} imposed {structural_adjustment_policy} on {debtor_nation}, forcing {privatization/austerity/export_orientation} that benefited {metropolitan_capital} while devastating {domestic_sector}. Show how conditionalities prevent {sovereign_policy} necessary for {autonomous_development_goal}, proving these institutions function as collective imperialist apparatus. Contrast with {nation}'s resistance through {alternative_mechanism}.

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Reproduces European Marxist dismissal of lumpenproletariat as counter-revolutionary in contexts where colonial under-development creates massive unemployed/underemployed populations excluded from formal exploitation
critique_patterns.fix: Recognize that in {colonized_context}, {lumpenproletariat} constitutes not marginal layer but majority excluded from formal wage labor by {colonial_underdevelopment}. Show how {revolutionary_movement} organized {specific_lumpen_strata} by linking their dispossession to {imperialist_mechanism}, as Fanon theorized and {historical_example} demonstrated, rather than dismissing them as unreliable elements.

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Treats technological development as neutral force rather than recognizing how imperialist monopoly over advanced technology (especially capital goods production) maintains dependency and how technology embeds specific social relations
critique_patterns.fix: Show how {dependent_nation}'s reliance on {imperialist_nation} for {technology/capital_goods} creates dependency through {mechanism: proprietary systems/planned obsolescence/monopoly pricing}. Demonstrate how technology embeds {social_relation} by analyzing how {specific_technology} requires {labor_process/skill_monopoly} controlled by {foreign_capital}. Contrast with {self-reliant_approach} that developed {alternative_technology} appropriate to {local_conditions} and sovereign control.

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Dismisses nationalism as inherently bourgeois based on European experience, ignoring how national liberation from imperialism is prerequisite for socialist construction in colonized contexts and how revolutionary nationalism differs from comprador nationalism
critique_patterns.fix: Distinguish revolutionary nationalism of {liberation_movement} fighting {imperialist_power} from comprador nationalism of {reactionary_regime} serving empire under national rhetoric. Show how {revolutionary_nationalism} united {class_alliance} against {colonial_extraction}, established sovereignty over {resource/sector}, and created conditions for {socialist_construction}. Demonstrate that internationalism in {colonized_context} means solidarity with anti-imperialist struggles, not abstract unity with metropolitan working class benefiting from super-exploitation.

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Analyzes trade as mutually beneficial exchange rather than recognizing how price disparities between primary commodities and manufactured goods systematically transfer value from periphery to core
critique_patterns.fix: Calculate how {colonized_nation} exports {quantity} of {commodity} worth {hours_labor} but receives manufactured goods worth {fewer_hours_labor}, revealing value transfer of {amount} annually. Show how this unequal exchange is maintained through {mechanism: monopoly pricing/currency manipulation/debt servicing}. Demonstrate that 'development' within this structure means intensified exploitation, as {historical_example} shows, requiring {break_mechanism} to achieve genuine accumulation.

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Celebrates Green Revolution as humanitarian achievement without analyzing how it increased dependency on imperialist agribusiness, destroyed food sovereignty, and enriched rural elites while immiserating poor peasants
critique_patterns.fix: Show how Green Revolution in {nation} created dependency on {corporation}'s seeds/fertilizers/pesticides, requiring {foreign_exchange} and debt to {imperialist_institution}. Analyze how {technology_package} benefited {kulak_class} with irrigation/capital while marginalizing {poor_peasant_strata}, leading to {dispossession_mechanism}. Contrast with {revolutionary_land_reform} that achieved {food_sovereignty_outcome} by breaking landlord power and imperialist agribusiness control.

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Treats natural resources as national endowments for development rather than analyzing how resource curse operates through imperialist control of extraction, processing, and pricing that prevents sovereign industrialization
critique_patterns.fix: Trace how {resource} in {nation} is extracted by {foreign_corporation}, processed in {imperialist_nation}, and sold back as manufactured goods at {markup}, preventing local value-addition. Show how {mechanism: concession_contracts/technology_monopoly/transport_control} locks {nation} into raw material export. Demonstrate how {nationalization_attempt} was sabotaged through {intervention_method}, and how {successful_case} achieved sovereignty by controlling entire commodity chain from {extraction} to {final_product}.

historical_context: Emerged from the contradictions of mid-20th century decolonization movements that revealed classical Marxism's inadequacy for analyzing societies never fully integrated into capitalist relations but subjected to colonial extraction. Crystallized through China's break with Soviet revisionism (1960s), the Cuban Revolution's challenge to both US imperialism and peaceful coexistence (1959-), and the Vietnamese defeat of French then American forces (1945-1975). Synthesized Mao's analysis of semi-feudal societies, Lenin's theory of imperialism as capitalism's highest stage, and Fanon's recognition that the 'wretched of the earth' constituted a new revolutionary subject. Gained theoretical coherence through dependency theory's demonstration that underdevelopment was actively produced by metropolitan accumulation, not a pre-modern residue. The Tricontinental Conference (1966) and Non-Aligned Movement formalized this paradigm's rejection of both US capitalism and Soviet social-imperialism. Lin Biao's 'Long Live the Victory of People's War' (1965) theorized the global countryside (third world) encircling global cities (imperial core). Revolutionary defeats in Indonesia (1965), Chile (1973), and Grenada (1983) alongside neoliberal counterrevolution forced reassessment of strategies for maintaining sovereignty while embedded in imperialist world-systems. Post-Soviet era saw paradigm's evolution through Bolivarian socialism, Bolivia's indigenous movements, and debates over whether China represents socialist construction or a new form of dependent development.

branch_metadata.synthesis_prompt: blend of dependency theory, Maoism, thirdwordism focused on questions of liberation from imperialism and colonialism
branch_metadata.additional_thinkers: Mao, Mariategui, Che Guevara, Fidel Castro, Ho Chi Mihn

description: Analyzes social life through creative action, technical normativity, and the constitutive role of material practice, critiquing the reduction of human activity to communication
guiding_thinkers: György Márkus, Hans Joas, John Dewey, G.H. Mead

assumptions: Human beings are fundamentally makers - homo faber precedes homo loquens
Technical activity has its own normativity not reducible to communicative reason
Creativity is a dimension of all action, not just exceptional moments
Tools and artifacts mediate between humans and world constitutively
Practice is prior to theory - understanding emerges from doing
Language is one form of symbolic mediation among others, not the master key
core_tensions: Work vs Communication - productive activity versus linguistic interaction
Technical vs Communicative Rationality - making things work versus reaching understanding
Creativity vs Routine - novel action versus habitual reproduction
Individual vs Social - personal creativity versus collective practices
scope_conditions: Applies to all forms of human activity, not just discourse
Requires attention to material practices and technical competence
Focus on situated action in concrete contexts

primary_entities: Praxis - purposive human activity transforming both world and actor
Technical Normativity - standards of correctness internal to material practices
Creative Action - action that generates genuinely new possibilities
Habit - embodied dispositions that enable and constrain action
Situation - the concrete context that calls forth and shapes action
relations: Tool Mediation - artifacts enabling and shaping human capacities
Skill Acquisition - embodied learning through practice
Problem-Response - action arising from problematic situations
Expressive Completion - action realizing inchoate impulses
levels_of_analysis: Bodily-practical - embodied skills and material engagement
Institutional-social - organized practices and collective action

change_mechanisms: Creative response - novel solutions to blocked action
Tool innovation - new artifacts enabling new practices
Habit transformation - reconstruction of settled dispositions
temporal_patterns: Skill development - from conscious effort to embodied mastery
Social learning - transmission and transformation of practices
transformation_processes: Reconstruction - reorganizing experience in response to problems
Democratic experimentalism - collective testing of social arrangements
Technical progress - development of productive capacities

key_concepts: Technical Normativity - standards governing whether practices achieve their aims
Creative Action - action not determined by prior conditions or rules
Situation - the problematic context calling forth inquiry and action
Objectivation - human capacities externalized in artifacts and institutions
Communicative Reification - false reduction of all reason to discourse
Means-End Holism - ends and means reciprocally constitute each other
analytical_methods: Genetic reconstruction - tracing how practices emerged and evolved
Situational analysis - understanding action in its concrete context
Technical critique - evaluating practices by their internal standards
Comparative pragmatics - examining different forms of practical reason
problem_diagnosis: Communicative reification - treating discourse as the only form of reason
Work denigration - devaluing productive activity relative to speech
Technical alienation - loss of understanding of how things work
Creativity suppression - social forms blocking novel action
ideal_state: Integrated praxis - unity of making, doing, and speaking
Technical democracy - shared control over productive processes
Creative society - institutions enabling rather than blocking novelty
Educated competence - widespread technical understanding

trait_definitions.trait_description: Attention to purposive, transformative human activity
Standards internal to practices of making and doing
Focus on genuinely novel, non-determined action

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Treating all rationality as reducible to discourse or communication
critique_patterns.fix: Identify the technical-practical rationality in {activity} irreducible to {speech_act}

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Ignoring or devaluing productive labor in analysis
critique_patterns.fix: Examine how {phenomenon} depends on {material_practice} and {technical_skill}

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Explaining action solely through prior causes or rule-following
critique_patterns.fix: Show how {action} involves creative response to {problematic_situation}

critique_patterns.diagnostic: Treating tools and artifacts as neutral means
critique_patterns.fix: Analyze how {artifact} shapes and enables {human_capacity}

historical_context: Synthesizes classical pragmatism with Marxian praxis philosophy, developed particularly in Márkus's 'Language and Production'
